questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to learn a language by watching TV
The work of subtitling, including sounds
Funny mistakes made on live television
Why deaf people watch less television
questions.why: They meet subtitler Karli Witkowska to find out more about subtitling.

questions.q: What does Beth say about dramatic, action-packed scenes?
options: They don't need any subtitles at all
They have the most dialogue of any scene
No one may speak, but sounds need describing
They are the easiest scenes to subtitle
questions.why: She says there might be no-one speaking, but all the sounds need to be described as well.

questions.q: Why is subtitling live TV harder?
options: It must be done as the person speaks
It must be translated into many languages
It uses more difficult and technical words
It is written months before the show airs
questions.why: Beth says live TV subtitling has to be done in the moment, as the person is speaking.

questions.q: How can subtitles help language learners?
options: They correct the learner's grammar mistakes
They slow down the speech so it's clearer
They show only easy words and phrases
You can read a word and hear it at once
questions.why: They let you read a word and hear how it's pronounced at the same time.

questions.q: What does Karli base her choice of words on?
options: The age of the audience
The genre and style of the show
The length of the scene
What the director tells her
questions.why: She says 'it depends on the genre and depends on the shows'.

questions.q: What has changed since the growth of streaming services like Netflix?
options: Subtitles are no longer needed
Subtitles are now written by computers
Subtitling has become something of an art
Only foreign films have subtitles
questions.why: Neil says since the growth of streaming, subtitling has become something of an art.

questions.q: Why did Karli love the description 'gobsmacked silence'?
options: It was short, clear and easy to read
It was her own idea, not her boss's
It described a loud scream in the scene
It showed shock, though there was no sound
questions.why: She says people were on the verge of a gasp, 'but there wasn't actually a sound'.

questions.q: How did Karli feel when her colleague thought of it?
options: She wanted to congratulate him
She was jealous
She wanted to change it
She was surprised it went viral
questions.why: She says she wanted to give him a virtual high five.
